title: Imran Khan to challenge FRRO’s directive asking him to leave India by Oct 28; veteran Raza Murad slams him for taking part in protest
raw_summary:
Actor Imran Khan, an American citizen and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder, is set to challenge the Foreigners Regional Registration Office’s (FRRO) directive asking him to leave India by October 28, as per a report by NDTV. His lawyer, Zulfiqar Memon, will file a petition before the Bombay High Court contesting the order.

The actor came under scrutiny following his participation in a protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Mumbai. The demonstration called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Following the protest, BJP (Bharatiya Janata Party) leader Kirit Somaiya lodged a complaint with the police, alleging that Imran Khan’s participation in the demonstration violated the restrictions applicable to foreign citizens. The police subsequently forwarded the complaint to the FRRO, which issued a notice directing the actor to leave the country.

The FRRO’s position is that holding an OCI card does not permit a foreign national to participate in protests. The order has been issued under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. Section 7 of the legislation empowers the Central Government to issue orders and directions regulating, restricting or prohibiting the entry, departure, presence or movement of foreign nationals in India.

Meanwhile, veteran actor Raza Murad has slammed Khan, asserting that foreign nationals should not interfere in India’s domestic affairs. He also defended the authorities’ handling of the matter, pointing out that the actor has been given time to respond to the order and can seek judicial intervention if he believes the decision is unjust.

“Whether it is Imran Khan or anyone else, no foreign national has any business interfering in the internal affairs of our country. I have only just learned that Imran Khan has become a U.S. national; he was an actor here. As a U.S. national, he has no right to participate so actively in the country’s internal affairs or its politics. The Mumbai Police are acting strictly within the legal framework,” Murad told the news agency ANI.

He further noted that the actor has been given 15 days and can approach the court if he believes he is being treated unfairly or is being compelled to leave the country.

“He has been given a full 15 days. If he feels he is being treated unfairly or being forced to leave the country, he is welcome to approach the court, and whatever the court decides, we must all accept it. Let’s see how he reacts. He has two options: either leave the country by October 28, or if he does not wish to leave, or feels that he has been wronged or treated unjustly, he can take his grievance to the court,” Murad added.

Imran Khan’s proposed legal challenge will now bring the dispute before the Bombay High Court, where the validity of the FRRO’s order can be contested.

title: Kiss Ka Kissa: Vidhi Kasliwal announces romantic short film starring Priyanshu Painyuli and Vandana Josh
raw_summary:
In a city where couples can stay connected over their phones all day but struggle to find a few uninterrupted minutes together, even a simple kiss can turn into an adventure. Exploring this idea is Kiss Ka Kissa, an upcoming romantic Hindi short film starring real-life couple Priyanshu Painyuli and Vandana Joshi. Landmarc Entertainment, led by filmmaker-producer Vidhi Kasliwal, has announced that the film will be released on October 22, 2026.

Set in Mumbai, Kiss Ka Kissa explores the romantic dreams people carry from their younger days and the little moments that sometimes remain unfulfilled. Combining humour, affection and everyday situations, the film looks at modern relationships and the ways romance can be found in seemingly ordinary experiences.

The pairing of Priyanshu Painyuli and Vandana Joshi, who are also a couple in real life, brings an element of familiarity to the story. Rather than relying on grand romantic gestures, the film focuses on the emotions that emerge from everyday interactions. At its core, it celebrates spontaneity in love and the small moments that bring two people closer.

For Vidhi Kasliwal, the project continues her interest in stories centred on human emotions. Her filmmaking journey includes working with Rajshri Productions alongside Sooraj R. Barjatya before making her writing and directorial debut with Isi Life Mein.

"What drew me to Kiss Ka Kissa was its simplicity. We often associate romance with grand gestures, but sometimes the smallest moments carry the deepest emotions. There is something wonderfully relatable about two people trying to find a little space for themselves in a city that never slows down. At Landmarc, we have always believed that stories don't need to be larger than life to touch lives. They simply need to feel real," says Vidhi Kasliwal.

Written and directed by Ashish Sharma, Kiss Ka Kissa marks his fiction debut following more than a decade of work in advertising films, music videos and branded storytelling. The film is presented by Landmarc Entertainment and produced under its Landmarc Films banner. Vidhi Kasliwal has handled the production and creative direction, while Aarti Bagdi serves as the creative producer.

Speaking about the film, Ashish Sharma shares, "I wanted to make Kiss Ka Kissa for two reasons: the little romantic dreams we carry from our younger days, and the joy of telling a simple, feel-good story. A first kiss, a stolen moment, a romantic adventure—sometimes life moves on, leaving these little dreams unfinished. Set against the chaos of Mumbai, the film explores how even the simplest romantic gesture can become an adventure when privacy is a luxury. I wanted the humour to emerge naturally from everyday situations. At its heart, the film celebrates love, youthful innocence and life's delightful unpredictability. I hope it leaves audiences smiling and perhaps remembering a little unfinished romantic story of their own."

Over the past 15 years, Landmarc has developed a filmography that includes Sanngto Aika, Vazandar, Ringan, Gachchi, Redu, Pipsi, Nashibvaan and Medium Spicy. As the company transitions into Landmarc Entertainment, it is expanding its operations through three initial verticals: Landmarc Films, Landmarc Melodies and Landmarc Digital. The company aims to explore new storytelling formats and support new voices while continuing to focus on emotionally driven narratives.

The film's creative team includes Vidhi Kasliwal as producer and creative visionary, Ashish Sharma as director, Aarti Bagdi as creative producer, Vikrant Thakur as director of photography and Puloma Pal as editor. Sarthak Karkare has composed the music, written the lyrics and created the background score. Prince Kumar of Casting Cubicle is responsible for casting, while K. R. Mahadevan [Mohan] serves as executive producer.

With its title reflecting the story's central idea, Kiss Ka Kissa looks beyond the kiss itself to explore the circumstances surrounding it. Against the pace of Mumbai, the film highlights how finding time for romance can be challenging, and how a single moment can become meaningful when two people make the most of it.

title: Nushrratt Bharuccha undergoes spine surgery, discharged from hospital; team shares health update
raw_summary:
Actor Nushrratt Bharuccha has been discharged from the hospital after successfully undergoing spine surgery following an accident in Bali earlier this month. Her team shared the update, confirming that the procedure went well and that the actor has returned home to continue her recovery.

In a statement, her team said, “After going through a difficult and challenging phase following her unfortunate accident, Nushrratt Bharuccha has successfully undergone spine surgery. We are relieved to share that the surgery went well, and she has now been discharged from the hospital.”

The statement added that Nushrratt is now at home, where she will focus on healing and regaining her strength. While her surgery was successful, her team noted that her recovery would take time.

“Nushrratt is finally back home, surrounded by care and comfort, as she begins the important journey towards recovery. While the road to complete recovery will take time, she remains positive and is focusing on healing and regaining her strength,” the statement read.

Her team also thanked fans and well-wishers for their support during this period. “We sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming love, concern, prayers and good wishes extended to her during this difficult time,” the statement added. Nushrratt Bharuccha’s accident and recovery Nushrratt was on a work-cum-holiday trip to Bali when the accident occurred around October 1. Her team initially described the incident as an “unfortunate accident”, without disclosing details about its exact cause.

Following the incident, the actor was treated and kept under observation at a hospital in Bali. She was subsequently airlifted to Mumbai by air ambulance for further evaluation and corrective spine surgery.

In the days following the incident, Nushrratt also shared glimpses of her recovery through Instagram Stories. One post featured a reclining wheelchair placed beside a window overlooking a sunset, accompanied by the caption, “Been chasing sunsets forever, And just like that… my view changed. But, Picture abhi baaki hai mere dost.”

In another update, the actor shared a picture of herself smiling in bed while watching the song ‘Gerua’ from Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol’s film Dilwale. The post carried the message, “Healing slowly, dreaming endlessly.”

With her team now confirming her discharge, Nushrratt has returned home and begun the next phase of her recovery. Further details about her recovery timeline have not been shared.

title: Niti Taylor recalls casting couch ordeal with Telugu film director: “You will have to sleep with me for it this time”
raw_summary:
Television actress Niti Taylor has opened up about a disturbing experience from the early years of her acting career, recalling an alleged casting couch incident involving the director of her debut Telugu film. In a candid conversation with Hauterfly, the actress revealed that the filmmaker approached her for another project after they had completed their first film together, but the conversation took an unexpected and deeply uncomfortable turn.

Recounting the incident, Niti said the director allegedly made an inappropriate demand in exchange for offering her another role. Describing how she reacted to the proposition, the actress said, "The director who did the first film with me called me for another movie when we were done with it. Then he said, 'But you will have to sleep with me for it this time.' You do not realise, you do not know how to react. I just cut the call, I blocked his number, I called up my mom, and I'm like, imagine that buddha, old man."

Niti further explained that although she had previously noticed the filmmaker behaving in ways she found questionable around other women, she had not anticipated being subjected to such a proposition herself. The incident left her so shocked that she decided to distance herself from the film industry.

Reflecting on how the experience affected her professional choices, she added, "I saw him with other chicks and stuff like that. I never knew when he would try this with me. That's when I decided I would never do any movies ever again. I was just taken aback, and I only blocked him. I did not tell this to anyone because I was zapped. You just come like..."

Niti made her Telugu film debut in 2012 with the romantic drama Mem Vayasuku Vacham, directed by Trinadha Rao Nakkina and produced by Bekkam Venugopal. Following the experience she described, the actress shifted her focus towards television, where she went on to establish herself as a familiar face among Indian audiences.

She rose to widespread popularity for playing Nandini Murthy in the youth-oriented series Kaisi Yeh Yaariaan, opposite Parth Samthaan. The show's popularity led to multiple subsequent seasons, further strengthening her fan following. Over the years, Niti has also appeared in television shows including Ghulaam, Ishqbaaaz and Bade Achhe Lagte Hain 2. She was last seen in the Amazon Prime Video reality series Alliance.

Her latest account offers a glimpse into the difficult experiences she says shaped her early career and influenced her decision to concentrate on television rather than pursue further film projects at the time.

title: Ramayana international trailer to be unveiled at Bengaluru event; Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi to attend
raw_summary:
Bengaluru is set to host the international trailer launch of Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana today, October 15, with Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Rocking Star Yash, Ravi Dubey, composer A.R. Rahman and director Nitesh Tiwari expected to attend the event along with other members of the cast and crew.

The event, hosted by Prime Focus Studios and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, comes as Sony Pictures begins its international campaign for the two-part epic ahead of its worldwide theatrical release. The international trailer will be unveiled in the presence of the film’s leading cast and creative team. Ramayana international trailer to be unveiled in Bengaluru The Bengaluru event marks the beginning of the film’s wider international promotional campaign, with Sony Pictures handling its global distribution outside India. The campaign is aimed at taking the Indian epic to audiences across international markets ahead of the first instalment’s theatrical release.

Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama in the film, while Sai Pallavi essays Sita. Yash will be seen as Ravana, with Sunny Deol playing Hanuman and Ravi Dubey portraying Lakshman. A.R. Rahman is among the composers associated with the project, with Nitesh Tiwari directing the film. Ramayana to release in two parts Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part film series. The first part is scheduled to release worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second instalment is set to arrive during Diwali 2027.

The film is scheduled to release across India in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam. It will also be presented in IMAX.

Sony Pictures will distribute Ramayana internationally, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will handle distribution in the Hindi-speaking market.

With the international trailer set to be unveiled today, the Bengaluru event is expected to offer a closer look at the scale and visual treatment of the upcoming adaptation before its theatrical release next month.

title: Kartik Aaryan and Sreeleela’s Anurag Basu-directed film locks April 30, 2027 release date
raw_summary:
Kartik Aaryan and Sreeleela’s upcoming romantic musical, directed by Anurag Basu, has locked April 30, 2027 as its theatrical release date. The untitled film is produced by T-Series’ Bhushan Kumar and Krishan Kumar, with music composed by Pritam.

The project marks Kartik and Sreeleela’s first on-screen collaboration and is also Sreeleela’s Bollywood debut. The actress, who has primarily worked in South Indian cinema, gained wider attention in Hindi-speaking markets following her appearance in the song 'Kissik' from Pushpa 2. Kartik Aaryan and Sreeleela headline an intense romantic musical The film is described as an original love story with music playing a central role in the narrative. While details about the plot remain under wraps, the project is not part of the Aashiqui franchise, despite earlier speculation linking Kartik to the popular romantic musical series.

The film has also been associated with the reported title Tu Meri Zindagi Hai, although an official title is yet to be announced.

Promotional glimpses released so far have featured Kartik in a rugged singer or rockstar avatar, with the actor seen performing with a guitar. The visuals have also offered glimpses of his romantic pairing with Sreeleela.

Directed by Anurag Basu, the film brings together the filmmaker’s storytelling with Pritam’s music and a lead pairing that is new to the Hindi film industry. April 30 release gives Kartik-Sreeleela film a clear window The April 30, 2027 release date places the film in a window without another major Hindi release currently announced for the same day. It arrives nearly three weeks after SS Rajamouli’s Varanasi, starring Mahesh Babu and Priyanka Chopra Jonas, which is scheduled for release on April 7, 2027.

The next major releases currently lined up are Lag Jaa Gale, starring Tiger Shroff, Lakshya and Janhvi Kapoor, and the Sourav Ganguly biopic DADA, both scheduled to arrive on May 14, 2027.

The release date therefore gives the Kartik Aaryan and Sreeleela starrer a clear theatrical window before the next set of major releases in May.

The project is an important release for Sreeleela as she makes her entry into Bollywood with a leading role opposite Kartik. The actress has established herself in Telugu and Kannada cinema and has featured in several South Indian films.

title: Kirti Kulhari’s production debut Kinaare to premiere at Dharamshala International Film Festival
raw_summary:
Acclaimed actor Kirti Kulhari is all set for a career milestone as she takes her maiden feature production, Kinaare, to the upcoming edition of the Dharamshala International Film Festival (DIFF).

Written and directed by the Qadri brothers (Akbar & Azam Qadri), Kinaare will premiere at DIFF and it marks a deeply personal chapter for Kulhari as she steps into the role of a producer. She has backed the feature under her banner Kintsukuroi Films along with co-producers Abhishek Koka and Maansi Guptey.

Led by an ensemble principal cast featuring Kulhari alongside Rajeev Siddhartha, Alka Amin, and Ravi Taneja, the film promises an intimate, lingering cinematic experience.

Set against the backdrop of a village near Delhi, Kinaare follows Amina (played by Kulhari), a single woman whose life is devoted to caring for her aging parents and tending to her home. Her routine is upended by a surprise visit from her cousin brother (Azam) after 15 years—unearthing a past that once fractured the family. Catching up on lost years—and love—the visit leaves her more at peace with the past and acceptance of the present.

Reflecting on the creative energy that went into shaping the project, lead actor and producer Kulhari shared, “Kinaare is a film that happens to be my first child as a producer, and that will always remain special. It’s a script that really resonated with me. It’s a simple, heartwarming, and subtle film. I find all these adjectives in Iranian films—which I’ve always really loved—so when something like this came to me, I knew I had to make it.”

Kulhari, who comes armed with more than a decade of a stellar acting career, said producing is not an easy task, especially if one’s trying to make a film themselves.

“This is exactly how I wanted to make this film: independently, make it the way I see it, the way we all see it collectively. It’s amazing that each and every member of the film has come together, believing in the script, and stood by my side purely for the passion of cinema, for the sole reason of being a part of the film for what it is. So, I’m very proud and happy to have brought something like Kinaare for the world to see.”

Echoing this sentiment, co-star Rajeev Siddhartha opened up about the rare rhythm of the script and the immersive environment on set.

“I feel every actor looks forward to and hopes that they come across a script where not only is the written word important, but also the script itself encourages you to explore the spaces between the words. And with Kinaare, I got to do that as an actor. I feel Kinaare has such a universal theme that everybody who sees it will definitely be touched, be moved and be slightly changed from within after the experience.”

Rounding out the film's artistic vision are cinematographer Arjun Sundaram, music composer Mohan Kannan, editor Bakul Matiyani, and sound designer Sanjay Chaturvedi.

title: Rajpal Yadav deposits Rs 2 crores in cheque bounce case; Supreme Court refers dispute to mediation
raw_summary:
The Supreme Court on Thursday referred Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav’s long-running cheque bounce dispute with Murli Projects Private Limited to mediation after he deposited Rs 2 crores with the Court as part payment of the outstanding dues. The Bench asked both parties to explore an amicable settlement for the remaining amount.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi noted that Yadav had earlier proposed selling his ancestral property to arrange the balance payment. The Court, however, said the parties should attempt to resolve the dispute through mediation before proceeding further with the matter.

The actor and the counsel representing Murli Projects agreed to the proposal. The case has now been referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre. Supreme Court asks Rajpal Yadav and complainant to explore settlement During the hearing, the Bench observed that Yadav had reached a point where he was considering selling his ancestral property to settle the case. The Court said it wanted both sides to explore an amicable resolution, while noting that it could still examine the matter on merits if required.

"What we are saying is that you have been brought to the verge of selling your ancestral property only to get rid of this case. Of course, we will hear on merits also, if the occasion arises. But at this stage, after losing before different courts, the scope of interference is known very well. We want that you amicably settle," the Court remarked.

In its order, the Bench recorded that mediation could help resolve the dispute. It stated, "Going by the issues briefly raised on behalf of the parties, it seems that the matter can be amicably resolved through mediation. Consequently, the parties have agreed to mediation before the Supreme Court Mediation Centre."

The Court directed both sides to approach the mediation process with an open mind and make an effort to reach a settlement over the remaining dues. It also permitted Yadav to seek the release of his passport for professional travel abroad, subject to the conditions imposed by the trial court. Rajpal Yadav deposits Rs 2 crores after proposing sale of ancestral property The payment follows an undertaking Yadav made before the Supreme Court during the previous hearing on October 7. At the time, the actor appeared in person and submitted demand drafts totalling Rs 1.15 crore.

His counsel informed the Court that a prospective buyer of Yadav’s ancestral property would deposit an additional Rs 85 lakhs, taking the total amount to Rs 2 crores. The remaining dues, the counsel submitted, would be arranged through the sale of the property.

The Court had taken note of the proposal and indicated that it would consider setting a schedule for payment of the balance amount. Following the deposit of Rs 2 crores, however, the Bench decided to refer the parties to mediation to explore a settlement.

The latest order does not mean that the dispute has been resolved. The parties will have to attempt to reach an agreement on the remaining amount through the mediation process. What is the cheque bounce case against Rajpal Yadav? The dispute stems from financial arrangements linked to Ata Pata Laapata, Yadav’s 2012 film. According to the case details, Yadav and his wife received Rs 5 crores from Murli Projects in connection with the film, which was being produced by the actor.

After the film could not be completed within the agreed timelines, the parties entered into a series of four agreements to address the dispute.

Under the third agreement, Yadav provided eight security cheques to Murli Projects. This agreement was subsequently replaced by a consent agreement dated April 21, 2013. According to Yadav’s plea, the later agreement provided for the return of the eight security cheques and the issuance of four fresh cheques worth Rs 10 crores each.

Yadav has alleged that Murli Projects did not return the original security cheques and instead presented seven of them for payment. The cheques were dishonoured, leading to criminal complaints against the actor and his wife.

In his plea before the Supreme Court, Yadav argued that the subsequent consent agreement had rendered the earlier cheques invalid. On that basis, he contended that the complaints filed under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act were not maintainable.

title: Suniel Shetty joins Marzi by Primus as brand ambassador to promote active ageing
raw_summary:
Marzi by Primus, a lifestyle and community platform for adults aged 50 and above, has announced actor, entrepreneur and fitness enthusiast Suniel Shetty as its brand ambassador, reinforcing its mission to transform how India experiences life beyond 50. Built around the belief that growing older should mean more freedom, discovery and fulfilment, Marzi encourages people to pursue their passions, make new friends, travel, stay active and enjoy life on their own terms.

Through its platform, Marzi brings together like-minded individuals through curated meet-ups, interest-based communities, social events, fitness activities and learning experiences. Marzi Travel extends this philosophy beyond everyday experiences, offering thoughtfully curated domestic and international holidays that bring people together through shared adventures, new destinations and meaningful connections. Together, these offerings seek to make active ageing an enriching and aspirational lifestyle.

The association is being launched through a new advertising campaign featuring Suniel Shetty, highlighting the joy of finding people who share one’s interests and passions. The film concludes with the message: “Be where you belong. With Marzi meet-ups, find your kind.”

Speaking about the association, Suniel Shetty, actor, entrepreneur, and brand ambassador for Marzi by Primus, said: “My age is a fact. How I choose to live is entirely up to me. At 65, I’m still learning, exploring new opportunities, staying fit and discovering new passions. And I’ve realised that a fulfilling life isn’t just about physical fitness. It’s about friendships, shared experiences, travel and having something exciting to look forward to. That’s what I love about Marzi. It encourages people to keep exploring, connecting and enjoying life on their own terms. Because the best years of your life don’t have to be behind you.”

Adarsh Narahari, Founder, Marzi by Primus, said: “For too long, ageing in India has been associated with slowing down, dependency and retirement. We believe it should be about freedom, discovery and new beginnings. At Marzi, we’re creating opportunities for people to make new friends, travel the world, discover new interests and lead more fulfilling lives. Suniel embodies this philosophy throughhis commitmentto fitness, constant reinvention and enthusiasm for life. We’re delighted to have him join us in inspiring India’s Generation Evergreen to live life on their own terms.”

The partnership marks another step in Marzi’s ambition to reshape the narrative around ageing in India, moving the conversation beyond healthcare and retirement towards experiences, friendships, wellbeing and the joy of living.

title: EXCLUSIVE: CBFC censors 57 seconds of Yami Gautam Dhar's dialogue in Nayyi Navelli; inserts disclaimer in visuals of masala eating
raw_summary:
Yami Gautam Dhar, who was recently in the news for winning the National Award for Article 370 (2024), will be seen on the big screen in Nayyi Navelli. It releases tomorrow, Friday, October 16, and has caught attention thanks to the horror comedy genre, entertaining trailer and casting of Yami. Earlier this week, the makers completed the censor process and in this article, Bollywood Hungama will exclusively focus on the same.

The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) passed Nayyi Navelli with a U/A 16+ certificate. However, they asked for a few minor changes. The Examining Committee (EC) of the CBFC asked the makers to redraft the opening disclaimer. The disclaimer now consists of the fact that the film is a work of fiction and that the makers abide by the rules.

A visual in the climax was 'suitably modified' while at the same time, the background music was also asked to be 'suitably modified'. Similarly, a dialogue of Mohini (Yami Gautam Dhar) was also asked to be 'suitably modified, wherever it occurred'. As a result, 57 seconds of her dialogue was censored.

Moreover, a static was added in the visual of masala eating, wherever it occurred. Lastly, the makers were asked to add anti-drug disclaimer in the beginning of the film.

Once these changes were made, Nayyi Navelli was passed by the CBFC on October 12. The length of the film, as mentioned on the censor certificate, is 138.00 minutes. In other words, Nayyi Navelli is 2 hours and 18 minutes long.

Besides Yami Gautam Dhar, Nayyi Navelli also stars Addinath M Kothare, Anurag Thakur, Sunita Rajwar and others.

title: Vidya Balan to open Indian Film Festival of Perth as chief guest in January 2027
raw_summary:
The inaugural Indian Film Festival of Perth (IFFP) will be held from January 22 to 24, 2027, with actor Vidya Balan announced as the Chief Guest. She will officially open the first edition of the festival, which aims to introduce audiences in Western Australia to the diversity of Indian cinema.

The festival marks a new addition to the celebration of Indian films in Australia. It is being organised by the team behind the Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (IFFM) and the Indian Film Festival of Sydney (IFFS). With established platforms in Melbourne and Sydney, the Perth edition aims to expand the reach of Indian cinema, provide opportunities for filmmakers and audiences to connect, and strengthen cultural ties between India and Western Australia.

The announcement of the festival coincided with the visit of Western Australia's Premier, Hon Roger Cook MLA, to India. The initiative reflects the growing cultural and creative links between the two regions and aims to encourage further cultural exchange through cinema.

Vidya Balan, known for her work across a range of roles and narratives, has been associated with films that explore distinctive stories and women-led characters. Her participation as Chief Guest at the inaugural festival will mark the beginning of the event, which seeks to bring audiences together through Indian cinema across languages, cultures and regions.

Speaking about the announcement, Mitu Bhowmick Lange AM, Festival Director, said, “Bringing the Indian Film Festival to Perth is a very special milestone for us. Having built platforms for Indian cinema in Melbourne and Sydney, we are delighted to now bring this celebration to Western Australia and connect with a new community of audiences and film lovers. Cinema has a remarkable ability to bring people together, transcend borders and create a deeper understanding of one another. We are thrilled to welcome Vidya Balan as the Chief Guest for our inaugural edition, and we look forward to creating a festival that celebrates the extraordinary diversity of Indian storytelling while building meaningful cultural connections between India and Western Australia.”

Through its first edition, the Indian Film Festival of Perth aims to establish a platform for Indian cinema in Western Australia and bring together film enthusiasts, filmmakers and members of the creative community. The programme will showcase stories from across Indian languages, genres and perspectives, while providing opportunities for discussions, collaborations and cultural exchange.

The festival's launch adds another platform for Indian cinema in Australia, with the organisers looking to build connections between audiences and the film industry while highlighting the range of stories emerging from India.

title: BREAKING: Ramayana is Ranbir Kapoor's second film after Animal to be 3 hours+; gets PG-13 rating in USA

The grand Diwali release, Ramayana, is three weeks away from release, and the excitement is steadily building up with each passing day. It's going to have the biggest release for an Indian film ever globally and the makers have been steadily working towards it. In a significant development, the censor process in the United States of America has been completed.

The Motion Picture Association has passed Ramayana with a PG-13 rating. This rating is similar to U/A in India and means that some material maybe inappropriate for children below the age of 13.

As per the Motion Picture Association website, Ramayana was awarded the said rating due to 'sequences of strong violence and action, and some bloody images'.

The other major development is that Ramayana has been passed internationally with a runtime of more than 3 hours. As per the website of IMAX, the duration of the film is 3 hours and 15 minutes. However, as per trade sources, the English version of Ramayana is expected to be shorter, at around 2 hours and 45 minutes. A clearer picture on this front will emerge in a few days.

Ramayana is Ranbir Kapoor's immediate release after Animal (2023). Incidentally, it is also the second film of his career, after Animal, to have a duration of more than 3 hours.
